newsitem.title: UK: ECC looks to cut costs after H1 profits crash.
newsitem.headline: ECC looks to cut costs after H1 profits crash.

text.p: English China Clays Plc said on Monday it needed to make more cost cuts after turning in a sharp fall in half year profits which dragged its shares down, but added that there were signs of improvement in its markets.

The company, which among other activities supplies minerals and chemicals to the paper industry, said in a statement that a current strategic review had "highlighted the need for significant cost reduction in the U.S. and European operations."
ECC's pretax profits for the six months ending June 30 crumpled to just 5.7 million pounds ($8.87 million) from 55.3 million pounds previously. It kept its dividend payout at 5.5 pence a share.
The company made an exceptional provision of 18.6 million pounds as a result of the continuing review in relation to some under-performing assets in Europe, the Pacific and Brazil.
ECC said the fall in profits was due to a drop in demand for minerals from the paper industry and a high level of costs of a semi-fixed nature along with manufacturing problems in the U.S.
It had warned in July that trading conditions had continued to be "severe" during the second quarter because of low output at paper mills.
ECC shares were down seven pence to 219-1/2 pence by 0846 GMT after touching a year-low of 217 pence earlier.
"People are going to sit on the sidelines until we see physical signs of the paper cycle turning which we haven't seen yet," said Nick Wilson, diversified industrials analyst at Kleinwort Benson.
ECC said trading conditions since June had not been "significantly different from the first half," and that in paper, "the position is mixed, depending on market segment."
But it did proffer some optimistic views.
ECC said it was seeing signs of improvement for minerals in Europe and steady performance in North America.
It said ceramics also continued to perform steadily worldwide. And cost cutting initiatives taken in the first half were already showing benefits, ECC said.
The company added that it would make a decision on the final year dividend based on the outcome of the review and trends in trading. ($1=.6430 Pound)
